Verdict: **PASS for the static, pure captured-module presentation policy only**.
There are no blocking performance findings in the reviewed source. Runtime
measurements, full application validation, startup, memory, responsiveness and
large-project behavior remain pending; this verdict does not establish them.

## Static findings

1. **Allocation and retained memory: PASS.** The resolver returns four borrowed
   `&str` values or a fixed typed error. The identity and result contain borrowed
   slices and small enums; copying them does not copy string bytes. There is no
   `String`, `Vec`, map, clone of owned data, allocation, cache or retained global
   state on the resolver path. Prefix/suffix results are slices into the captured
   external ID. Auxiliary memory is constant. Keeping the original captured
   strings alive is the caller's existing lifetime requirement, not new storage
   allocated by this policy. Debug/formatting performed by callers is outside
   this analysis.
2. **Per-module complexity and raw paths: PASS.** Non-Gradle, missing-capture and
   missing-project-ID branches do constant work. A source-set name needs at most
   one reverse search for the final ASCII colon. A project name compares the two
   optional reported paths directly, then optionally performs that same reverse
   search. In the worst case, work is O(P + I), where P is the path data compared
   and I is the external-ID data searched; auxiliary memory remains O(1). There
   is no repeated split collection, concatenation, filesystem normalization,
   canonicalization or path I/O. Long equal paths and colon-free IDs require
   linear inspection rather than constant time. UTF-8 metadata is borrowed and
   ASCII delimiter splitting does not require re-encoding.
3. **Startup and project scaling: PASS within scope.** The additive module export
   introduces no initializer, task, subscriber, scanner, import call, SDK/JVM
   invocation, UI work or startup hook. The resolver processes one captured
   identity and never enumerates projects, modules, folders or classes. An
   eventual caller applying it independently to N modules will spend work
   proportional to the total compared/searched metadata, rather than making
   this policy intrinsically quadratic. The future importer/controller and any
   repeated presentation evaluation need their own measured review.
4. **Crate, fixture and compile impact: PASS within scope.** Cargo dependencies,
   feature configuration and the build script are unchanged. The retained eight
   complete reference files total 264,942 bytes; the full new fixture/provenance
   directory contains 11 files totaling 285,677 bytes. The new policy and tests
   do not embed these fixtures with `include_str!`/`include_bytes!`, and the build
   script does not process them. They add repository storage rather than a new
   runtime payload or compiled JVM component. The source module and one new
   integration-test target do add bounded Rust compilation work; actual build
   time and resulting artifact sizes have not been measured here.
5. **Supplemental long-metadata test: PASS as static coverage.** The long-name
   case creates a 327,680-byte imported name in test setup and checks borrowed
   internal/sort/group pointers, plus the exact display suffix. That setup's
   allocations belong to the test. The colon near the end means this case does
   not exercise the longest delimiter-search path; it is a borrowing regression
   case, not a stress benchmark or allocation instrumentation. Existing short
   cases cover IDs without a delimiter and raw path comparison. No performance
   measurement or test pass is inferred from their definitions.

## Scope and pending evidence

No Cargo, Gradle, app, compiler, benchmark, cache mutation, SDK probe or native
measurement was launched. Root owns the exclusive runtime lease. The owner must
still record the required actual build/tests/clippy/format gates and applicable
runtime evidence, with the compiled source and executable identities bound to
this reviewed source. Whole-IDE and large-project performance are not rated by
this static review. No UI publication, authoritative identity import, Kotlin
capability detection or original reference-test parity credit is provided here.

Only this external review artifact was written. Product sources, fixtures,
canonical matrix and protected branches were not modified.
